## RCS Business Messaging

The future of SMS is here. RCS (Rich Communication Services) is the industry upgrade to traditional texting, allowing businesses to deliver richer, more interactive messages. Partner with EZ Texting to ensure your business always has first access to cutting edge features like RCS.

*   **Branded, Verified Sender.** Your business name, logo, and trust badges replace phone numbers which boosts recognition and open rates.
*   **Rich, Interactive Experiences.** Send carousels, buttons, quick replies, images, video, and transactional flows (orders, payments, appointments) within the conversation.
*   **Enhanced Security.** Messages travel over encrypted channels and verified sender routes, reducing spoofing risk.

## Getting Started with Your Text Marketing Campaign

STEP 1

### Secure a Trusted Number

Utilize trusted number options that are fully carrier-approved and compliant with industry regulations:

*   **Local Number (10DLC)**
*   **Dedicated Short Code**
*   **Toll-Free Number**
*   **Text-Enabled Landline**

STEP 2

### Build Attentive Audiences

Leverage customizable opt-in tools and segmentation features, ensuring that messages are delivered to a receptive audience interested in their offerings, thus maximizing engagement and conversion potential:

*   **Sign-Up Forms**
*   **QR Code Generator**
*   **Keywords**
*   **List Uploads**
*   **Double Opt-In**
*   **Opt-Outs**
*   **Workflows**
*   **Integrations**

STEP 3

### Craft Texts That Deliver

Manage and deliver impactful messages using a user-friendly interface, scheduling options, and analytics tools, guaranteeing optimized engagement and conversion rates:

*   **Mass Texts**
*   **Two-Way Texts**
*   **SMS & MMS**
*   **Text Templates**
*   **AI Compose**
*   **Team Inbox**

## Key Factors That Influence SMS Marketing Pricing

### Frequency of Messaging

The number of text messages you plan to send directly affects the cost of text marketing. At EZ Texting, each plan comes with 500 credits, plus the option to purchase more.

### Quantity of Contacts

Each outbound message uses credits per recipient, so larger audiences consume credits faster. EZ Texting plans scale with your list and include unlimited contact uploads, making it easy to grow.

### Message Type: SMS vs MMS

SMS messages (text only, 160 characters) are 1 credit each, and MMS messages (including images or video, and/or up to 1600 characters) are 3 credits each.

## Choosing the Right SMS Marketing Service

Not all SMS marketing services are created equal, and choosing the right SMS service is critical to success in your texting journey.

### Reliability & Compliance

Rely on our industry-leading delivery rates and consistent adherence to legal regulations to protect your brand’s reputation and customer trust.

### Feature Set & Scalability

EZ Texting offers versatile tools and the capacity to adapt to increasing messaging needs, enabling effective and expansive outreach strategies as your business expands.

### Cost-Effectiveness & ROI

Our affordable pricing plans, efficient campaign management tools, and analytics to measure performance empower you to optimize your SMS marketing strategies and achieve higher engagement and conversion rates without overspending.

## Powerful Integrations at Your Fingertips

Title: SimpleTexting vs EZ Texting (2026): Which Is Actually Cheaper?

URL Source: https://ddiy.co/simpletexting-vs-ez-texting/

Published Time: 2026-08-20T17:30:44+00:00

Markdown Content:
**EZ Texting starts at $20 a month. SimpleTexting starts at $29.**

If that settled it, this page would be one line long.

It does not settle it, because the two companies charge for completely different things. **EZ Texting bills you for how many people are on your list. SimpleTexting bills you for how many messages you send.**

So the cheaper option depends almost entirely on the size of your contact list, and the gap between them gets enormous in both directions.

The short answer

*   **Under 500 contacts:** EZ Texting Launch at $20/mo is genuinely cheaper
*   **Over 500 contacts:** SimpleTexting wins, and the margin widens fast
*   **The catch nobody reads:** EZ Texting’s 6,000 credits are per year, not per month
*   **Seats:** SimpleTexting includes 3 users, EZ Texting includes 1

Advertising Disclosure

## The Prices Side by Side

EZ Texting publishes four tiers. The price is set by your contact count. SimpleTexting publishes eight, set by credits, and our [SimpleTexting pricing guide](https://ddiy.co/simpletexting-pricing/) breaks each one down.

| EZ Texting plan | Price | Contacts | Credits | Users |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Launch | **$20/mo** | Up to 500 | 6,000/year | 1 |
| Boost | **$60/mo** | 500 to 2,000 | 6,000/year | 1 |
| Scale | **$100/mo** | 2,000 to 50,000 | 6,000/year | 1 |
| Enterprise | **From $3,000/mo** | 50,000+ | 200,000/month | Custom |

Those prices are the annual-billing rates. EZ Texting advertises up to 20% off for paying yearly.

**SimpleTexting has no named plans at all.** It runs nine tiers priced purely by how many credits you send in a month. One SMS up to 160 characters is one credit, an extended message up to 306 characters is 2, and an MMS is 3.

| Credits a month | Price | Per message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 500 | **$29/mo** | 5.8 cents |
| 1,000 | $49/mo | 4.9 cents |
| 2,000 | $79/mo | 4.0 cents |
| 3,000 | $109/mo | 3.6 cents |
| 7,500 | $229/mo | 3.1 cents |
| 15,000 | $399/mo | 2.7 cents |
| 25,000 | $549/mo | 2.2 cents |
| 50,000 | $899/mo | 1.8 cents |

That entry tier is **500 credits at $29 a month on a toll-free number**. A local number instead makes it $39 and adds a one-time $4 carrier registration fee that toll-free skips. Paying yearly saves 20%, and nonprofits get 15% off.

**Contacts are unlimited on every tier**, no matter which one you are on, and unused credits roll over to the end of the following month.

## They Do Not Charge for the Same Thing

This is the whole comparison, and almost every other article gets it wrong by lining the two prices up as though they measure the same quantity.

**EZ Texting sells you list capacity.** Moving from Launch to Boost triples your bill and buys you nothing except room for more contacts. The message allowance does not change.

**SimpleTexting sells you message volume.** Your list can be 200 people or 200,000 and the price is identical. What moves the price is how many texts you send.

So the question is not “which is cheaper.” It is **which of your two numbers is bigger**: your list, or your send volume.

## The 6,000 Credits Are a Yearly Allowance

Here is the detail that catches people out.

EZ Texting’s Launch, Boost and Scale plans all include **6,000 credits per year**. Not per month.

**That works out to 500 messages a month**, which is exactly the same allowance as SimpleTexting’s $29 entry bundle. The two headline numbers look twelve times apart and describe identical volume.

It also means the Scale plan at $100 a month ships the same 6,000 credits as the Launch plan at $20. You are paying five times as much purely for contact headroom.

**What happens when you run out.** EZ Texting charges overage per message: 4 cents on Launch, 3.5 cents on Boost, 3 cents on Scale, and 1 cent on Enterprise.

SimpleTexting has no overage charge, because you simply move up a credit tier instead. Going from 500 to 1,000 credits costs $20 more, which works out to 4 cents for each extra message. The step from 1,000 to 2,000 is $30 for 1,000 credits, or 3 cents each.

**So the marginal cost is roughly the same on both**, somewhere between 3 and 4 cents. The difference is that EZ Texting starts charging it after 6,000 messages a year, while SimpleTexting’s allowance is monthly.

Free calculator

## What will SMS marketing actually cost you?

These six platforms charge for completely different things. Three sell message credits, one bills by the size of your list, one sells prepaid credit up front, and one is pure pay as you go. Set your numbers below and see all six ranked on what you would actually pay.

Assume a modest 500 messages a month, which both entry offerings cover without overage. The only variable is list size.

**The crossover sits at 500 contacts.** That is the ceiling on EZ Texting’s cheapest plan, and the moment you pass it your bill triples while SimpleTexting’s does not move at all.

At 60,000 contacts the comparison stops being a comparison. EZ Texting pushes you into a quote-only Enterprise plan starting at $3,000 a month. SimpleTexting still charges $29, because it never cared how long your list was.

**Flip it around and EZ Texting wins.** A 300-contact list you text three times a week is roughly 3,900 messages a month. That is heavy send volume on a tiny list, which is the shape EZ Texting prices well and SimpleTexting does not.

results.title: Stop Unwanted Robocalls and Texts
results.markdown:
Title: Stop Unwanted Robocalls and Texts

URL Source: https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/stop-unwanted-robocalls-and-texts

Markdown Content:
Robocalls are more than an annoyance, they are often the preferred tool of fraudsters. Stopping illegal robocalls is the Federal Communication Commission’s (FCC) top consumer protection priority.

To restore trust in our phone networks, the FCC is fighting illegal robocalls at every point of a call's journey, from its source to your phone.

This includes empowering carriers to block more illegal robocalls before they reach consumers, giving consumers better tools to distinguish legitimate calls from scams, stepping up enforcement, and disrupting scam calls that originate outside of the United States.

![Image 1: Man holding a smartphone with a green and red call button on screen.](https://www.fcc.gov/sites/default/files/robocalls_illustration_guide.png)

Scammers often use [caller ID spoofing](https://www.fcc.gov/spoofing) to make their calls appear legitimate so you are more likely to answer. If you think the call has been spoofed, don't hang on, hang up!

## **How to avoid phone scams**

Scammers create a false sense of urgency and leverage technology and information they can find online to sound convincing.

*   Don't answer calls from numbers you don't know.
*   Hang up right away if someone asks for money or personal information.
*   If you feel pressured, or a caller asks you to pay with gift cards, it's a scam!
*   Never share account numbers, Social Security numbers, passwords, PINs, or other important information over the phone.
*   If someone says they're calling from a company or a government agency, hang up and call back using an official phone number from an account statement (if you have one) or their website.
*   Don’t respond to texts or click on links sent from numbers you don’t recognize.
*   Set up strong passwords for your voicemail so it doesn’t get hacked.
*   Talk to your phone company about call blocking tools they may have and check into apps that you can download to your mobile device to block unwanted calls.

[Check the FCC Scam Glossary](https://www.fcc.gov/scams) for detailed breakdowns of specific robocall scams. Help us spread the word by talking to your family and friends about phone-based scams.

## **Robocalls rules**

Robocalls are phone calls made using an autodialer or a prerecorded or artificial voice message.

FCC rules require a caller to obtain your prior written consent – on paper or through electronic means, including website forms or a telephone keypress – before they make a prerecorded telemarketing call to your home or wireless phone number. FCC rules also require a caller to obtain your oral or written consent before making an autodialed or prerecorded call or text to your wireless number.

These rules do not apply to emergency calls about danger to life, safety, or property.

#### **Types of permitted autodialed calls**

FCC rules allow market research or polling calls and calls on behalf of tax-exempt non-profit groups to landline numbers. Calls about school closings or flight information are also permitted to your landline.

#### **Opting out of autodialed calls**

Prerecorded telemarketing calls must provide an opt-out option at the start of the message. You may opt out of any robocall or robotext at any time and in any reasonable manner, even if you previously gave consent for such calls.

#### **Prerecorded voice messages**

All prerecorded voice message calls must include the caller's name, number, and business name at the beginning of the message.

#### **Artificial intelligence and voice cloning**

AI-generated voice calls are illegal unless the consumer has agreed to receive them or the caller is exempt.

#### **Telephone solicitations**

Telephone solicitations are calls that act as an advertisement. Phone solicitations are permissible with prior express permission or from tax-exempt non-profits. Telemarketing calls based on an established business relationship are not permitted to your landline phone without your advanced permission.

## **Robotexts**

FCC rules ban text messages sent to a mobile phone using an autodialer unless the phone owner previously gave consent to receive the message or the message is sent for emergency purposes.

Commercial texts require written consent; for informational texts, your consent may be oral.

FCC rules apply even if you have not placed your mobile phone number on the [National Do Not Call Registry](https://www.donotcall.gov/).

#### **Tips for avoiding text**[**scams**](https://www.fcc.gov/scam-glossary)**and spam**

*   Do not respond to texts from unknown or questionable sources, and never click links in these messages.
*   Most mobile carriers let you block spam by forwarding the message to 7726 (SPAM)—check with your provider.
*   Be careful about giving out your mobile phone number and personal information.
*   Before submitting your number on websites, read the privacy policy and look for opt-out options—often a checkbox.
*   Check the policies of the companies you do business with for selling or sharing your information.

## **Political campaign robocalls & robotexts**

The Telephone Consumer Protection Act contains specific rules callers must follow when making campaign calls or sending texts:

*   **Landlines:** Political robocalls (autodialed or prerecorded) are allowed without prior consent.
*   **Cell phones:** Political calls, texts, or prerecorded messages require the recipient’s prior permission—unless sent manually.
*   **Robotexts:** Autodialed political texts need consent; manually sent texts do not.
*   **Caller Identification:** Prerecorded or artificial voice calls must begin with the caller’s name, phone number, and the name of the organization they represent (if calling on behalf of a third-party).

## **Filing complaints about robocalls and texts**

**FCC Complaints**: You can [report](https://www.fcc.gov/complaints) illegal calls or texts to the FCC. Choose the “unwanted calls” category and note if your number is being spoofed, blocked, or mislabeled.

**What Happens Next**: The FCC doesn’t resolve individual complaints but uses them to guide policy and possible enforcement under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act or the Truth in Caller ID Act. Your complaint may also be shared with other enforcement agencies.

**FTC Complaints**: [Report](https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/#/?orgcode=FCC) phone scams or Do Not Call violations to the FTC.

### **File a complaint with the FCC**

If this consumer guide does not address your issue, you have the option to file a complaint.

[Start your complaint](https://consumercomplaints.fcc.gov/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=39744)

![Image 2: Computer screen icon](https://www.fcc.gov/sites/default/files/computer_phone_complaint_b.png)

## **Do Not Call Registry**

The [National Do Not Call Registry](https://www.donotcall.gov/) is a list of landline and wireless phone numbers that legitimate telemarketers agree not to call. You can register your numbers for free at [donotcall.gov,](http://www.donotcall.gov/ "Do Not Call Registry Home Page") or by calling 1-888-382-1222 (TTY: 1-866-290-4236). You must call from the phone number you wish to register.

Under FCC rules, telemarketers calling your home must provide their name along with the name, telephone number, and address where their employer or contractor can be contacted. Telemarketing calls to your home are prohibited before 8 a.m. and after 9 p.m., and telemarketers must comply immediately with any do-not-call request you make during a call.

#### **Other do-not-call lists**

Many states now have statewide do-not-call lists for residents. Contact your state's [public service commission or consumer protection office](https://www.naruc.org/about-naruc/our-mission/regulatory-commissions/) to find out if your state has such a list and how you can sign up.

## **FCC actions to protect consumers**

*   Issued hundreds of millions of dollars in enforcement actions against illegal robocallers.
*   Empowered phone companies to block suspected illegal calls.
*   Allowed phone companies to block numbers not on a customer's contact list or "whitelist" when the customer opts in.
*   Required [caller ID authentication](https://www.fcc.gov/call-authentication) to reduce illegal spoofing.
*   Mandated blocking of illegal international robocall traffic.
